findings.evidence: test_c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py:946-1001 (test_T15_detachment_nonaliasing_and_source_effects). The names, identities and deep-copied container state snapshots (lines 949-954) are taken from FIX['r2'] only when T15 starts. unittest runs methods in name order, so T02-T14 have already called FIX['prepare'] hundreds of times by then. T15's success input is the same fresh K6 input T02 uses (line 958; T02 lines 815-817), and its refusal inputs are exactly T14_CASES + CASE_CARDANO_ANCHOR (line 981), already used in T14 (line 938) and T13 (lines 588-605). An r2 that mutates a module-level dict/list in place on first use (for example a content-keyed memo of VK digests or statement headers) would be warm before the snapshot. T15's state comparison (lines 989-994) and the held-container checks (lines 995-998) would then pass. The 'global' token scan (lines 250 and 1007-1009) catches only rebinding. S33 CP07 forbids caching and global mutation, and the T15 row requires 'module namespace keys and mutable globals unchanged'.
findings.requiredFix: In T15, after the leading _prepare() call, exec a fresh r2 module from FIX['r2_bytes'] with _module against the pinned FIX['host'] (sys.modules unchanged, no proxy; T01 sets the precedent). Take the names/identities/container-state snapshot of that fresh module before its first call, and route every T15 success and refusal call through the fresh module's prepare_c2_issue. Keep _prepare() as T15's first statement. Then re-freeze the bytes and obtain a fresh review of the changed bytes before any root RED. findings.evidence: test_c2_issue_artifacts_r2.py:160-169 catches FileNotFoundError around the whole _read(R2_FILE, 131072) call. _read (lines 91-104) runs os.open at line 92 outside its inner try/finally, then fstat (94), os.read (98) and os.close (104) on the open descriptor. S33 section 7 requires both 'r2 is read by the same _read' and 'Only FileNotFoundError from that exact open'. On Linux only the path-based open can raise ENOENT: O_NOFOLLOW symlinks give ELOOP, non-regular files and oversize raise AssertionError without the phrase at lines 95 and 102, and other errors propagate. The comment at lines 161-164 matches this effective behaviour.
findings.requiredFix: No fix is required for the reviewed ROOT RED scope; the contract is satisfied operationally. Optional tightening in the F1/F2 revision: inside the except clause, re-raise unless error.filename == os.path.join(HERE, R2_FILE). A descriptor-level error carries filename None, so only the exact r2 open can then produce MISSING_R2, and the same _read is kept.

findings.evidence: PROPOSED-ORDINARY-ENVELOPE.json argvTemplate: --unshare-all (new net namespace), --ro-bind /usr and --ro-bind ROOT_PINNED_555_ENVELOPE /input, --clearenv plus PATH/LANG/PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, prlimit cpu 10, as 536870912, fsize 2097152, core 0, timeout 10s with kill-after 2s, python3 -I -B. A malicious r2 could raise text containing MISSING_R2, but r2 is absent at RED.
